items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn’t hear – I don’t know what Conrad Janis really ever sounded like.

ctx.x: May I interrupt again? How did the Down Beat thing happen? How did it actually occur that you wound up writing for Down Beat?

The regular stringer left to do something else – be a promoter, I think. I guess it must have been Norman Granz or somebody like that who knew me – or Nat Shapiro – one of the New Yorkers who came through Boston and heard the radio show and told whoever was editing Down Beat at the time, why don’t you try this guy Hentoff? Then I got to be a columnist there, because I was so controversial. There was one of Rudi Blesh’s people, Conrad Janis. They were the revivalists. I once wrote that they were so careful to…
What were some of the other controversial things that you wrote that got the letters to the editors coming in?
